Grade a single exercise file against its tests

Source: R/grade.R
grade_exercise.Rd

Sources the student's file and the matching test file into an isolated environment, runs every function whose name starts with test_<exercise>_, and returns the per-test outcome as a grade_results object.

Usage

grade_exercise(
  file,
  test_dir,
  timeout = 10,
  student = NA_character_,
  engine = c("callr", "inproc"),
  allow_masking = character()
)

Arguments

file

Path to the student's file: an R script (e.g. "ejercicio1.R") or an R Markdown or Quarto document (.Rmd, .qmd), whose R chunks are extracted with knitr::purl(). The matching test file is found ignoring case.

test_dir

Directory that contains the test files.

timeout

Maximum seconds allowed per test function, and for loading the student's file. Tests that exceed it are recorded with status timeout. Default 10. Use Inf for no limit.

student

Optional student display name. Defaults to NA.

engine

"callr" (default) runs each exercise in a fresh R subprocess via the callr package, with a temporary working directory. The timeout is a hard wall-clock limit, and assignments with <<- or files the student writes do not reach your session or folder. "inproc" runs tests in the current R session. It is faster, but its setTimeLimit() timeout does not interrupt every kind of loop, and student code can see and change your global environment.

allow_masking

Character vector of function names from base R and the default packages (stats, utils, methods, graphics, grDevices) that the student may redefine, e.g. "factorial" when the exercise asks for it. Any other student object with such a name is not visible to the tests, so a student cannot pass by redefining all() or ==. Ignored names are listed in the message column.

Value

A grade_results object with one row per test. If the student file fails to parse, one row with status = source_error. If no matching test file is found, one row with status = missing and a warning.

Details

A test passes if it returns TRUE. Tests can also use testthat expectations (call library(testthat) at the top of the test file): the test passes when at least one expectation succeeds and none fails, and a failed expectation is recorded as fail with its message.

Examples

# The package ships test files for five sample exercises.
tests <- system.file("examples", package = "corrector")
file <- file.path(tempdir(), "ejercicio1.R")
writeLines(c(
  "ceros_cuadratica <- function(a, b, c) {",
  "  d <- sqrt(b^2 - 4 * a * c)",
  "  c((-b - d) / (2 * a), (-b + d) / (2 * a))",
  "}"
), file)
grade_exercise(file, tests, student = "Garcia")
#> <grade_results> 4 rows, 1 students, 1 exercises
#> Status:
#>   pass          3
#>   fail          1
